I was watching some youtube video, when I saw [this thing](https://i.sli.mg/mbCTTp.png) hover over the middle top of the video, and it acted as some sort of pop-out display. I thought this was made by yt itself, but I found no real use to it (other than progress bar can be controlled on the display, that it stays always on top and that it can be re-sized at one's pleasure), but cool nonetheless.

Now I was checking v/gifs and it surprised me that appeared on HTML5 gifs as well (slimg and imgur links that end with a v as in .gifv, webms, gfycats). The neat thing is that it lets me pause and go to any part of the gif with the progress bar, same as with a video. This is specially good for long gifs, although there aren't that many.

Then I looked at Opera's changelogs, and lo and behold:

>[Video pop out displays video in a floating frame, always on top.](http://www.opera.com/docs/changelogs/unified/3700)

I'm not an Opera shill pushing my Opera agenda, I just kind of found this out of the blue and wanted to share it with Voat, but I do like Opera overall, specially with the mute button they added a few months ago.

Gifs will never be as good as videos, but with each passing day they're more *like* videos.
